en: 2 eggs
A handful of fresh spinach
2 tbsp light cream or yogurt
1 tbsp grated Gruyère
Salt, pepper, nutmeg
Wilt the spinach in a pan 2 minutes and drain it
Spread it in the ramekin with the cream and seasoning
Crack the eggs on top and sprinkle the cheese
Bake in a water bath 12 minutes at 180°C
2 slices wholegrain bread
1 egg
100 ml low-fat milk
A pinch of cinnamon and vanilla
1 tsp honey, a handful of berries
Whisk the egg with the milk, cinnamon and vanilla
Soak each slice for a minute per side
Cook in a non-stick pan 3 minutes per side
Serve with the honey and fresh berries
2 eggs and 2 egg whites
Low-fat ham or turkey, diced, 40 g
Low-fat grated Gruyère cheese 20 g
Low-fat milk 2 tbsp
A little salt and black pepper
Chopped parsley for garnish (optional)
Whisk the eggs and egg whites with the milk, salt and black pepper.
Add the ham and cheese, mix well.
Pour the mixture into a small lightly greased oven-safe dish.
Bake at 180°C for 18-20 minutes until set and golden, garnish with parsley if desired and serve warm.

name.en: Whole Grain Buckwheat Crêpes with Berries

en: Buckwheat flour 40 g
1 egg
Low-fat milk 120 ml
A pinch of salt and 1 tsp oil for the pan
Fresh mixed berries (strawberries and blueberries) 80 g
Honey 1 tsp to serve (optional)
Whisk the buckwheat flour with the egg, milk and salt until a smooth, lump-free liquid batter forms.
Heat a non-stick pan with a little oil over medium heat.
Pour a thin layer of batter, cook for a minute until the edges dry, flip and cook the other side for 30 seconds.
Repeat with the remaining batter, serve the crêpes with fresh berries and honey if desired.
2 eggs and 2 egg whites
Fresh mushrooms, sliced, 80 g
Chopped spring onion and 1 crushed garlic clove
Low-fat milk 2 tbsp
Chopped fresh chives and parsley 1 tbsp total
A little salt and black pepper
Brown the mushrooms, spring onion and garlic in a dry pan for 4-5 minutes until cooked and the moisture evaporates.
Whisk the eggs and egg whites with the milk, salt and black pepper.
Mix the browned mushrooms and herbs into the egg mixture, pour into a small oven-safe dish.
Bake at 180°C for 18-20 minutes until set and golden, serve warm.

name.en: Whole Grain Brioche French Toast Cups

en: Whole-wheat brioche bread, cubed, 60 g
1 egg and 1 egg white
Low-fat milk 100 ml
A pinch of ground cinnamon and vanilla extract half a tsp
Brown sugar 1 tsp
Light maple syrup 1 tbsp to serve (optional)
Distribute the brioche cubes into lined muffin tins.
Whisk the egg and egg white with the milk, cinnamon, vanilla and brown sugar.
Pour the mixture over the bread cubes and press gently to soak, let it sit 10 minutes.
Bake at 180°C for 18-20 minutes until set and golden, serve with maple syrup if desired.
2 eggs and 2 egg whites
Zucchini, sliced thin, 80 g
Low-fat feta cheese, crumbled, 30 g
Chopped spring onion
Low-fat milk 2 tbsp
A little chopped fresh mint, a little salt and black pepper
Whisk the eggs and egg whites with the milk, salt and black pepper.
Add the zucchini, feta, spring onion and mint, mix well.
Pour the mixture into a small oven-safe dish.
Bake at 180°C for 20-25 minutes until set and golden, serve warm.

name.en: Whole Grain Yogurt Waffles with Fruit Compote

en: Whole-wheat flour 50 g
Low-fat Greek yogurt 60 g and 1 egg
Low-fat milk 60 ml and baking powder half a tsp
A pinch of vanilla extract
Apple or pear, diced, 100 g for the fruit compote
A pinch of ground cinnamon and honey 1 tsp for the fruit compote
Mix the flour, yogurt, egg, milk, baking powder and vanilla until a smooth, thick batter forms.
Heat the waffle iron, pour in half the batter and cook according to the appliance instructions until golden and crisp, repeat with the remaining batter.
In a small pot, cook the apple with the cinnamon, honey and 1 tbsp water over medium heat 7-8 minutes until soft.
Serve the waffles with the warm fruit compote on top.

name.en: Baked Smoked Salmon and Herb Egg Cups

en: 2 eggs and 2 egg whites
Smoked salmon, cut into small pieces, 40 g
Chopped fresh dill and chives 1 tbsp total
Low-fat milk 2 tbsp
A little lemon juice and black pepper
A little salt (be mindful of the saltiness already in the salmon)
Whisk the eggs and egg whites with the milk, lemon juice, a little salt and black pepper.
Add the smoked salmon and herbs, mix gently.
Distribute the mixture into lined muffin tins about three-quarters full.
Bake at 180°C for 15-18 minutes until set and golden, serve warm.
Whole-wheat flour 60 g
Apple, cut into small cubes, 80 g
1 egg and low-fat milk 40 ml
Ground cinnamon 1 tsp and baking powder half a tsp
Honey 2 tbsp
A pinch of vanilla extract
Mix the flour with the cinnamon and baking powder in a bowl.
In another bowl, whisk the egg with the milk, honey and vanilla.
Combine the two mixtures until just combined without overmixing, gently fold in the apple cubes.
Distribute into lined muffin tins about three-quarters full, bake at 180°C for 20-22 minutes until golden on top, serve warm.
100 g tuna in water
1 boiled egg
100 g cooked green beans
Tomato, lettuce, black olives
1 tbsp olive oil, vinegar, mustard
Whisk the oil, vinegar, mustard and salt into a dressing
Arrange the lettuce, tomato and beans on the plate
Add the tuna, halved egg and olives
Pour the dressing just before serving
150 g cooked green lentils
1 carrot, 1 celery stick, 1 small onion, diced
1 tsp Dijon mustard
1 tbsp olive oil, wine vinegar
Parsley, salt, pepper
Whisk the mustard, vinegar, oil and salt
Toss the warm lentils in the dressing so they absorb it
Add the carrot, celery and onion
Finish with parsley, serve warm or cold
Whole-wheat bread, 2 slices (70 g)
Low-fat ham or turkey 50 g
Low-fat grated Gruyère cheese 40 g
Melted low-fat butter 1 tsp and whole-wheat flour 1 tsp for the béchamel
Low-fat milk 80 ml for the béchamel
A pinch of nutmeg, salt and black pepper
Melt the butter in a small pot, add the flour and stir for a minute.
Gradually add the milk while stirring constantly until the texture thickens, add the nutmeg, salt and black pepper.
Arrange the ham on a bread slice, pour half the béchamel, sprinkle half the cheese, cover with the other slice, pour the remaining sauce and sprinkle the remaining cheese.
Bake at 200°C for 12-15 minutes until the cheese melts and turns golden, serve hot.

name.en: Provençal Vegetable and White Bean Soup (Soupe au Pistou)

en: Canned white beans, drained, 100 g
Zucchini, carrot and green beans, diced, 150 g total
Diced tomato, chopped onion and 1 crushed garlic clove
Small pasta (coquillettes), cooked, 40 g
Chopped fresh basil 2 tbsp and 1 tsp olive oil for the pistou
Light vegetable stock 400 ml, salt and black pepper
Brown the onion and garlic in a dry pot for 3 minutes.
Add the carrot, zucchini, green beans and tomato, stir for two minutes.
Add the stock, salt and black pepper, cover and simmer 15-18 minutes until the vegetables are cooked.
Add the white beans and cooked pasta, cook 3 more minutes, mix the basil and oil for the pistou and drizzle over the soup when serving.
Thin whole-wheat pastry sheet, 1 piece (50 g)
Low-fat ham or turkey, diced, 50 g
2 eggs and 1 egg white
Low-fat milk 150 ml and low-fat grated Gruyère cheese 30 g
A pinch of nutmeg, salt and black pepper
Chopped spring onion for garnish (optional)
Roll out the pastry into a small lined tart tin.
Distribute the ham over the pastry.
Whisk the eggs and egg white with the milk, cheese, nutmeg, salt and black pepper, pour over the ham.
Bake at 180°C for 30-35 minutes until set and golden, garnish with spring onion if desired and serve warm.
Leek, sliced (white and light green parts), 150 g
Potato, diced, 150 g
Chopped onion and 1 crushed garlic clove
Light vegetable stock 400 ml
Low-fat milk 60 ml
Salt, black pepper and chopped parsley for garnish
Brown the leek, onion and garlic in a dry pot for 5 minutes until softened.
Add the potato and stock, cover and simmer 18-20 minutes until the potato is fully cooked.
Blend the soup with an immersion blender until smooth.
Add the milk, salt and black pepper, reheat without boiling, garnish with parsley and serve hot.
Thin whole-wheat pastry sheet, 1 piece (60 g)
Large onions, sliced very thin, 300 g total
1 crushed garlic clove and Provençal herbs half a tsp
1 tsp olive oil
Pitted black olives, halved, 1 tbsp for garnish
A little salt and black pepper
Brown the onion and garlic in a dry pan over medium-low heat 20-25 minutes, stirring, until caramelized and sweet.
Add the Provençal herbs, salt and black pepper.
Roll out the pastry on a lined tray, spread the caramelized onion over it.
Garnish with olives, bake at 200°C for 18-20 minutes until the edges are golden, serve warm.
Chicken breast 140 g
Low-fat Greek yogurt 2 tbsp
Chopped fresh tarragon 1 tsp and lemon juice 1 tsp
Dijon mustard half a tsp
Whole-wheat bread, 2 slices (70 g)
Chopped lettuce and sliced tomato to serve
Season the chicken with salt and black pepper, bake at 220°C for 15-18 minutes until fully cooked, let cool then slice.
Mix the yogurt, tarragon, lemon juice and mustard to make the sauce.
Spread the sauce on the bread slices.
Arrange the chicken, lettuce and tomato on one slice, cover with the other slice and serve.
Large tomatoes, hollowed out, 2 pieces (300 g)
Lean minced beef 100 g
Cooked rice 50 g
Chopped onion and 1 crushed garlic clove
Dried Provençal herbs half a tsp, salt and black pepper
Low-fat grated cheese 20 g for topping (optional)
Cut off the top of each tomato and set aside, gently hollow out the flesh with a spoon and reserve.
Mix the minced beef with the onion, garlic, rice, Provençal herbs, salt, black pepper and a little of the tomato flesh.
Stuff the tomatoes with the mixture, cover with their tops.
Arrange in a lined tray, sprinkle with cheese if desired, bake at 200°C for 30-35 minutes until cooked, serve hot.
Buckwheat flour 50 g
1 egg and low-fat milk 150 ml
A pinch of salt and 1 tsp oil for the pan
Fresh mushrooms, sliced, 80 g
Low-fat grated Gruyère cheese 40 g
1 extra egg for the filling and chopped parsley for garnish
Whisk the buckwheat flour with the egg, milk and salt until a smooth liquid batter forms.
Brown the mushrooms in a dry pan for 4-5 minutes until cooked and the moisture evaporates.
Heat a non-stick pan with a little oil, pour a layer of the batter to form a large thin galette.
Arrange the mushrooms and cheese in the centre, crack the extra egg on top, fold the four edges inward to form a square, cook 4-5 minutes until the egg is cooked, garnish with parsley and serve hot.
170 g skinless chicken
3 tomatoes, chopped
1 onion, 2 garlic cloves
Black olives, herbes de Provence
1 tbsp olive oil, salt
Brown the chicken in the oil on both sides
Add the onion and garlic, sauté 2 minutes
Add the tomatoes, herbs and half a cup of water
Cover and simmer 25 minutes, then add the olives
1 small aubergine, cubed
1 courgette and 1 bell pepper
3 tomatoes, chopped
1 onion, 2 garlic cloves
2 tbsp olive oil, thyme, basil
Fry the aubergine alone until golden and set aside
Sauté the onion and garlic, then the courgette and pepper
Add the tomatoes and thyme, cook 15 minutes
Return the aubergine, simmer 10 minutes, finish with basil
Cod fillet 140 g
Diced tomato and pitted black olives, 60 g total
1 crushed garlic clove and chopped onion
Dried Provençal herbs (thyme and rosemary) half a tsp
1 tsp olive oil and lemon juice 1 tbsp
Salt, black pepper and chopped parsley for garnish
Arrange the fish fillet on a lined baking tray.
Mix the tomato, olives, garlic, onion, Provençal herbs, oil and lemon juice, spread over the fish.
Sprinkle with salt and black pepper.
Bake at 200°C for 18-20 minutes until the fish is cooked and flaky, garnish with parsley and serve hot.
Skinless chicken thighs 140 g
Mushrooms, quartered, and sliced carrot, 150 g total
Small onions, quartered, and 2 crushed garlic cloves
Dry red wine 2 tbsp (alcohol cooks off during cooking)
Light chicken stock 250 ml and 1 tsp whole-wheat flour to thicken the sauce
Mixed herbs (thyme and bay leaf), salt and black pepper
Brown the chicken in a dry pot for 4-5 minutes on each side until golden, set aside.
In the same pot, brown the onion, garlic, mushrooms and carrot for 5 minutes.
Add the flour and stir for a minute, add the wine, stock, herbs, salt and black pepper.
Return the chicken to the pot, cover and simmer 25-30 minutes until the chicken is fully cooked and the sauce thickens.
Salmon fillet 140 g
Zucchini and carrot, cut into thin strips, 150 g total
1 crushed garlic clove and lemon juice 2 tbsp
1 tsp olive oil, salt and black pepper
Chopped fresh dill 1 tbsp
Baking paper for wrapping
Spread a large piece of baking paper on the work surface.
Arrange the zucchini and carrot strips in the centre, place the salmon fillet on top.
Mix the garlic, lemon juice, oil, salt and black pepper, pour over the salmon, sprinkle with dill.
Fold the paper tightly into a sealed parcel, bake at 200°C for 18-20 minutes, open carefully when serving.
Lean beef, cut into cubes, 140 g
Mushrooms, quartered, and sliced carrot, 150 g total
Small onions, quartered, and 2 crushed garlic cloves
Dry red wine 2 tbsp (alcohol cooks off during cooking)
Light meat stock 250 ml and 1 tsp whole-wheat flour to thicken the sauce
Mixed herbs (thyme and bay leaf), salt and black pepper
Brown the beef in a dry pot for 4-5 minutes on each side until golden, set aside.
In the same pot, brown the onion, garlic, mushrooms and carrot for 5 minutes.
Add the flour and stir for a minute, add the wine, stock, herbs, salt and black pepper.
Return the beef to the pot, cover and simmer 35-40 minutes until the beef is fully cooked and the sauce thickens.

name.en: Baked Duck Breast with Orange Sauce

en: Skinless duck breast 140 g
Fresh orange juice 80 ml and grated orange zest a pinch
Honey 1 tsp and balsamic vinegar 1 tsp
1 crushed garlic clove and dried thyme half a tsp
Salt and black pepper
Steamed broccoli 150 g to serve
Season the duck breast with salt, black pepper, garlic and thyme.
Heat a dry pan, cook the duck breast 3-4 minutes on the former skin side then 3 minutes on the other side, remove and let rest.
In the same pan, add the orange juice, zest, honey and balsamic vinegar, cook 3-4 minutes until the sauce thickens slightly.
Slice the duck breast, pour the sauce over it and serve with the steamed broccoli.
Lean pork tenderloin 140 g
Dijon mustard 1 tbsp and whole grain mustard 1 tsp
Low-fat Greek yogurt 2 tbsp
Light meat stock 100 ml
1 crushed garlic clove and dried thyme half a tsp
Salt, black pepper and cooked green beans 150 g to serve
Season the pork with salt, black pepper, garlic and thyme.
Brown it in a dry pan for 3-4 minutes on each side until golden, bake at 200°C for 12-15 minutes until fully cooked, let rest 5 minutes.
In the same pan, add the stock and both mustards, cook 2-3 minutes, reduce heat and add the yogurt, stir until the sauce is smooth without boiling.
Slice the pork, pour the sauce over it and serve with the green beans.
Sole fillet or similar white fish 140 g
Whole-wheat flour 1 tbsp for coating
Melted low-fat butter 1 tsp
Lemon juice 2 tbsp and grated lemon zest a pinch
Chopped fresh parsley 1 tbsp
Salt, black pepper and cooked asparagus 150 g to serve
Season the fish with salt and black pepper, coat with a thin layer of flour.
Arrange on a lined tray, brush with the melted butter.
Bake at 200°C for 12-15 minutes until cooked and flaky.
Pour the lemon juice and zest over it, sprinkle with parsley and serve with the cooked asparagus.

name.en: Turkey and Chestnut Stuffed Cabbage Rolls

en: Large cabbage leaves, lightly blanched, 4 leaves (150 g)
Lean minced turkey 120 g
Cooked chestnuts, coarsely chopped, 40 g
Chopped onion and 1 crushed garlic clove
Dried thyme half a tsp, salt and black pepper
Light meat stock 200 ml
Mix the minced turkey with the chestnuts, onion, garlic, thyme, salt and black pepper.
Place two spoonfuls of filling in the centre of each cabbage leaf, fold in the sides and roll tightly.
Arrange the rolls in an oven-safe dish, pour the stock over them.
Cover the dish and bake at 180°C for 40-45 minutes until the meat is fully cooked, serve hot.
150 g plain yogurt
1 tsp honey
10 roasted almonds, crushed
A pinch of cinnamon
A few drops of vanilla
Stir the yogurt with the vanilla
Spoon it into a small cup
Drizzle the honey over it in a spiral
Scatter the almonds and cinnamon, serve chilled
100 g low-fat fromage blanc
1 garlic clove, crushed
Fresh herbs (chives, parsley)
Juice of a quarter lemon
Carrot, cucumber, celery sticks
Mix the cheese with the garlic and lemon juice
Add the chopped herbs, salt and pepper
Chill 20 minutes so the flavours mingle
Serve with cold vegetable sticks
Whole-wheat flour 40 g
Low-fat butter 1 tsp and water 80 ml
1 egg
Low-fat grated Gruyère or parmesan cheese 30 g
A pinch of salt and a pinch of nutmeg
A pinch of black pepper
Heat the water with the butter and salt in a small pot until boiling.
Add the flour all at once and stir vigorously until a ball of dough forms that pulls away from the sides of the pot, let the dough cool 3 minutes.
Add the egg and mix well until combined, add the cheese, nutmeg and black pepper.
Shape small balls with two spoons on a lined tray, bake at 200°C for 18-20 minutes until puffed and golden, serve warm.

name.en: Radishes with Butter and Sea Salt

en: Fresh red radishes 150 g
Low-fat softened butter 2 tbsp
A pinch of coarse sea salt
Chopped parsley for garnish (optional)
Wash the radishes thoroughly and trim the leaves, leaving a little for decoration.
Cut each radish in half lengthwise.
Arrange on a serving plate, place the softened butter beside them.
Dip each radish half in the butter and sprinkle with sea salt, garnish with parsley if desired and serve immediately.
Whole-wheat flour 50 g
Cold low-fat butter, cubed, 2 tbsp
Low-fat grated parmesan or Gruyère cheese 30 g
1 egg
A pinch of salt and black pepper
A pinch of paprika (optional)
Mix the flour and cold butter with your fingertips until the texture is coarse crumbs.
Add the cheese, salt, black pepper and paprika if desired, mix well.
Add half the egg (reserve the rest for brushing) and knead until a cohesive dough forms, roll into a thin log and refrigerate 15 minutes.
Cut into 6 pieces, arrange on a lined tray, brush with the remaining egg, bake at 180°C for 15-18 minutes until golden, serve once slightly cooled.

name.en: Endive Boats with Blue Cheese and Walnuts

en: Belgian endive leaves, 4 large leaves (100 g)
Low-fat blue cheese, crumbled, 30 g
Coarsely chopped and toasted walnuts 1 tbsp
Honey half a tsp
Chopped parsley for garnish (optional)
Wash the endive leaves and dry them thoroughly.
Arrange them on a serving plate boat-style.
Distribute the blue cheese and toasted walnuts over each leaf.
Drizzle a little honey over them, garnish with parsley if desired and serve immediately.
Mixed green and black olives 80 g
1 crushed garlic clove and grated lemon zest a pinch
Dried Provençal herbs half a tsp
1 tsp olive oil
A pinch of chili flakes (optional)
Chopped parsley for garnish (optional)
Drain the olives from their brine if needed.
Mix them with the garlic, lemon zest, Provençal herbs, oil and chili flakes if desired.
Let the flavours infuse in the fridge for at least 30 minutes (an hour or more is best).
Garnish with parsley if desired and serve at room temperature.
Thin whole-wheat pastry sheet, 1 piece (50 g)
Low-fat grated parmesan or Gruyère cheese 30 g
Egg white for brushing
A pinch of paprika and a pinch of black pepper
A pinch of dried thyme (optional)
Roll out the pastry, brush with the egg white.
Sprinkle the cheese, paprika, black pepper and thyme if desired over half of it.
Fold the other half over it, press gently then cut into 6 long thin straws.
Arrange on a lined tray, bake at 200°C for 12-15 minutes until golden and crisp, serve once slightly cooled.

name.en: Baked Whole-Wheat Ficelles with Herb Butter

en: Whole-wheat flour 60 g
A pinch of instant yeast and warm water about 40 ml
A little salt
Softened low-fat butter 1 tsp
Chopped fresh parsley and chives 1 tsp total
A pinch of crushed garlic (optional)
Mix the flour with the warm water, yeast and salt gradually until a soft, cohesive dough forms, knead for 5 minutes.
Let the dough rest covered in a warm place 45-60 minutes until doubled in size.
Shape into two long thin sticks, place on a lined tray, let rest another 15 minutes.
Bake at 220°C for 15-18 minutes until golden, mix the softened butter with the herbs and garlic if desired and serve alongside.
Pear, cut into thick slices, 150 g
Low-fat Roquefort or blue cheese, crumbled, 30 g
Honey half a tsp
Coarsely chopped and toasted walnuts 1 tsp
A little lemon juice to prevent the pear browning
Brush the pear slices with a little lemon juice to prevent browning.
Arrange them on a serving plate.
Place a piece of Roquefort cheese on top of each slice.
Drizzle a little honey and sprinkle with the toasted walnuts, serve immediately.
150 g berries or pitted cherries
1 egg
100 ml low-fat milk
25 g wholewheat flour
1 tsp honey, vanilla
Whisk the egg, milk, flour, honey and vanilla
Spread the fruit in a greased baking dish
Pour the batter over the fruit
Bake 25 minutes at 180°C until just set
1 ripe pear, peeled
1 cup water or apple juice
1 cinnamon stick, 1 star anise
Lemon peel, cloves
1 tsp honey
Bring the water to a boil with the spices and lemon peel
Add the pear and lower the heat
Poach 20 minutes, turning so it colours evenly
Lift it out, reduce the liquid 5 minutes and pour it over
Thin whole-wheat pastry sheet, 1 piece (40 g)
Apple, sliced very thin, 150 g
A pinch of ground cinnamon and lemon juice 1 tsp
Brown sugar 2 tbsp
Melted low-fat butter 1 tsp
Light apricot jam 1 tsp for glazing (optional)
Roll out the pastry on a lined tray.
Arrange the apple slices over it in an overlapping circular pattern.
Sprinkle with cinnamon, lemon juice and brown sugar, brush with the melted butter.
Bake at 200°C for 20-22 minutes until the edges are golden and the apple is tender, brush with warm apricot jam if desired and serve warm.
2 eggs (whites only used)
Unsweetened raw cocoa powder 2 tbsp
Low-fat Greek yogurt 60 g
Brown sugar 2 tbsp
A pinch of vanilla extract
A pinch of salt
Whip the egg whites with a pinch of salt until stiff peaks form.
Mix the cocoa, yogurt, brown sugar and vanilla in a separate bowl until smooth.
Gently fold the whipped egg whites into the cocoa mixture in three additions until combined without losing the air.
Pour into serving cups and chill in the fridge for at least 2 hours before serving.
Thin whole-wheat pastry sheet, 1 piece (40 g)
Pear, sliced thin, 120 g
Ground almonds 20 g and brown sugar 2 tbsp
1 egg
Vanilla extract half a tsp
Sliced almonds for garnish 1 tsp (optional)
Roll out the pastry into a small lined tart tin.
Mix the ground almonds, brown sugar, egg and vanilla until combined, spread over the pastry.
Arrange the pear slices over the almond mixture in an overlapping pattern.
Sprinkle with sliced almonds if desired, bake at 180°C for 25-30 minutes until golden and the filling is set, serve warm.
Low-fat milk 200 ml
Low-fat Greek yogurt 60 g
Powdered gelatine half a tsp
Honey 2 tbsp
Vanilla extract 1 tsp
Fresh berries for garnish (optional)
Soak the gelatine in 2 tbsp cold water for 5 minutes until softened.
Heat the milk with the honey in a small pot until nearly boiling, remove from heat and add the soaked gelatine, stir until fully dissolved.
Add the vanilla and yogurt, mix well until the texture is smooth.
Pour into serving cups and chill in the fridge for at least 4 hours until set, garnish with fresh berries if desired and serve cold.
Low-fat milk 150 ml
1 egg and 1 extra egg yolk
Brown sugar 2 tbsp (1 for the mixture, 1 for the caramelized top)
Vanilla extract 1 tsp
A pinch of salt
Whisk the egg and extra yolk with 1 tbsp of the brown sugar, vanilla and salt.
Heat the milk in a small pot until nearly boiling, gradually pour it over the egg mixture while stirring constantly.
Pour the mixture into a small oven-safe ramekin, place it in a tray with hot water reaching halfway up the ramekin.

Bake at 160°C for 30-35 minutes until set (still slightly jiggly in the centre), chill in the fridge, sprinkle the remaining sugar over it and caramelize with a small torch or under the broiler just before serving.
Medium apples, peeled and quartered, 2 pieces (200 g)
Brown sugar 2 tbsp
Melted low-fat butter 1 tsp
A pinch of ground cinnamon
Thin whole-wheat pastry sheet, 1 piece (50 g)
Lemon juice 1 tsp
Mix the apple slices with the lemon juice and cinnamon.
Heat the brown sugar and butter in an oven-safe pan over medium heat until melted and lightly caramelized (3-4 minutes).
Arrange the apple quarters tightly over the caramel, cook 5 more minutes.
Cover the apples with the pastry and tuck the edges in, bake at 200°C for 20-25 minutes until the pastry is golden, carefully invert onto a serving plate while hot.
Ground almonds 40 g and whole-wheat flour 20 g
Fresh orange juice 60 ml and grated orange zest 1 tsp
1 egg and 1 egg white
Honey 2 tbsp and baking powder half a tsp
A pinch of vanilla extract
Sliced almonds for garnish 1 tsp (optional)
Whisk the egg and egg white with the honey until slightly foamy.
Add the orange juice, zest and vanilla, mix well.
Add the ground almonds, flour and baking powder, gently fold until the texture is combined.
Pour into a small oven-safe dish lined with baking paper, sprinkle with sliced almonds if desired, bake at 180°C for 25-30 minutes until golden and set, let cool before slicing.
2 egg whites
Powdered sugar 40 g
A pinch of salt and a little lemon juice
Fresh strawberries, sliced, 100 g
Low-fat Greek yogurt 60 g
A pinch of vanilla extract
Whip the egg whites with the salt and lemon juice until soft peaks form.
Gradually add the powdered sugar while continuing to whip until glossy and stiff.
Pipe or spoon small circles of the meringue mixture onto a lined tray, bake at 100°C for 90 minutes until fully dry, let cool.
Mix the yogurt with the vanilla, layer the crumbled meringue with the yogurt and strawberries in serving cups and serve immediately.
